chunks: They are those who reject the signs of their Lord, and the meeting with Him. So their good deeds will be fruitless, and on the Day of Judgement We shall not appoint any weighing for them.
ai.seo_question: Why are the deeds of disbelievers considered fruitless according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the futility of worldly deeds for those who deny the Hereafter, emphasizing that faith in 'meeting God' is the prerequisite for the acceptance of actions. The phrase 'we will not set up for them a scale' signifies a complete absence of divine accounting for their works, as their rejection nullifies the spiritual value of their efforts. This reflects the principle that belief in the afterlife is the foundation upon which the merit of all other deeds rests.
